source: NASA GES DISC, OMI/Aura OMNO2d v004 via Earthdata OPeNDAP (Earthdata Login)

variable.definition: The amount of NO2 gas, mostly from cars, power plants and industry, in the air between the ground and about 10 km up, counted as molecules above each square centimetre.

units_note: values are in molecules/cm^2; they are often reported in 1e15 molecules/cm^2
processing: OPeNDAP subset of 0.25° cells whose centres fall inside the bbox, one request per daily granule
daily box mean with cos(latitude) weights over valid cells; valid area fraction recorded
day used only if valid cells cover >= 50% of the box area
monthly value = mean of the used days' box means
month set to NaN if fewer than 10 days were used
trailing calendar month dropped if the granules stop before its last day
caveats: OMI row anomaly (since 2007, worse after 2009) removes part of the swath, so fewer valid days in later years; the affected rows are flagged and excluded in the product.
Cloud-screened: only retrievals with cloud fraction < 30 % are gridded, so cloudy days (frequent in winter) are missing and the monthly mean is a clear-sky mean.
Daily L3 has gaps (orbit gaps, missing granules, screening); months with too few valid days are dropped, more often in winter.
Aura overpass is about 13:30 local solar time: one early-afternoon snapshot per day, not a daily average; afternoon NO2 is lower than morning rush-hour NO2.
Tropospheric column (whole lower atmosphere), not ground-level concentration.
Aura has been drifting from its original orbit in recent years (later local overpass time); check the OMNO2 README before relying on the last years of the record.
